newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea changes base year for trade index.
newsitem.headline: South Korea changes base year for trade index.

text.p: South Korea has changed the base year for its trade index to 1995 from 1990 to better reflect changes in trading volume and prices, the central Bank of Korea said on Friday.
The bank statement said the unit prices would now be assessed on a quarterly basis from the previous yearly basis in order to get a more accurate figure.

Following the changes, South Korea's trade index according to export price competitiveness stood at 87.7 in 1996, against the previous 87.6. When the index goes below 100, it means the nation's price competitiveness has weakened from the base year.
The central bank said export unit price index changed to 86.6 for 1996, from 87.2, while import unit price index was at 98.8 compared with 99.6.
South Korea's trade index on a volume basis marked 105.0 last year from 104.2.
